subtype: Approach: choosing time, place and privacy [Action]
passage: Counsellor's note, third session. Francis arrived with a plan for telling his parents that he is moving to another city for work. Last month he had tried at a family lunch during a festival, and it had turned into a shouting match. This time he had thought about the setting. He went through his options with me: not during a festival, not on a stressful workday, not over the phone. He settled on a calm Sunday afternoon in the family living room, when both parents would be rested, with the tea already made. He asked whether to invite his aunt. We agreed it was better to be just the three of them. I did not write his words for him; I only asked what the setting would give them. He said, "Room to listen, not just react." He will tell me next week how it went. - Arohi

qa.q: When did Francis choose to talk to his parents?
qa.a: He settled on a calm Sunday afternoon in the family living room.

qa.q: What might Francis be feeling about the talk, given the shouting match last month?
qa.a: Francis is probably nervous and cautious, wanting to avoid the same outcome.

qa.q: What could Francis do if his parents still react strongly?
qa.a: Francis could pause and offer to continue another day, keeping things calm rather than pushing on.

qa.q: How might the setting help Francis's parents?
qa.a: They would be rested and calm, with room to listen instead of react.

grounding: Francis picks a calm Sunday afternoon in the living room, avoiding festivals and stressful workdays, so his parents can listen.
